transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Mark Daniels (HarborEdge CTO), Sara Liu (Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Second discovery focused on sizing and operational details for HarborEdge's Dedicated GPU capacity. Main concerns: single-tenant isolation, VPC/KMS integration, burst policy that respects PII constraints, warm pools and cold-start times, quantization tradeoffs, and a pilot benchmark. Agreed next steps: pricing options, schedule bench, share security docs and traffic distribution.

Topics:
- Baseline vs peak sizing
- Burst strategies: within-dedicated, private spare, or fallback to hosted (with restrictions)
- Security: SOC2, VPC, KMS, audit forwarding
- Benchmarks: p50/p90/p99 latency targets and embeddings throughput
- Onboarding timeline and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi all, thanks for taking the time again. Alex from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer is here. we'll confirm requirements and then plan a bench run.
[00:10] Mark Daniels: Hi Alex. we wanted to nail down the burst and compliance piece. some prompts are regulated, can't leave our VPC.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Understood. For those prompts we can set request-level policies to prevent logging and opt for private-only routing. Also Dedicated supports VPC peering so traffic never leaves your network for the single-tenant pool.
[00:31] Tom Reeves: If we need to burst beyond reserved GPUs, can we burst to a private spare pool that you manage but still sits in our region and complies with our controls?
[00:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we offer private spare capacity in the same region as an option. it's still isolated by tenant and can be configured with the same KMS keys and no-logs policy. otherwise, fallback to hosted variants is possible but only for non-sensitive workloads.
[00:54] Sara Liu: Good. about cold starts: what's realistic if a surge hits and we need extra instances up?
[00:59] Priya Rao: cold starts vary. for 70B models it can be up to 90 seconds, smaller 13B around 30s. we recommend a warm pool of idle workers for critical services which reduces effective scale time to seconds. continuous batching & KV cache also speed things up.
[01:18] Mark Daniels: For capacity planning, our baseline is roughly 80 QPS for short-chat tokens, peaks to 200-220. night embeddings run batches of ~10M vectors over a 2-3 hour window.
[01:29] Alex Chen: Based on that pattern, a reserved pool sized for 60-70th percentile plus burst for the top 10-20% is a common pattern. we'll propose a 4x-A100 equiv and an 8x-A100 equiv config and show cost/lateny tradeoffs.
[01:42] Tom Reeves: We need audit logs shipped to our Splunk instance and SAML SSO integration for RBAC.
[01:48] Priya Rao: Both supported. audit logs can be forwarded and we support SAML and fine-grained RBAC. we also have options to store logs in your S3 behind your KMS keys.
[02:00] Sara Liu: Evals: can bench runs include our prompt set and give regression detection over time with rollouts?
[02:06] Priya Rao: Yes. we'll run your prompts across model variants and quantization configs, compute regressions against baseline prompts, and set alerts tied to rollouts. we can demo Redwood Optimize outputs showing cost vs quality.
[02:19] Mark Daniels: Timeline if we agree: how long to provision and onboard models?
[02:23] Priya Rao: Typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated: infra, networking, KMS, model onboarding, and pilot bench. if you choose private on-prem it'll be longer.
[02:33] Alex Chen: We'll need your token distribution and sample prompts to size accurately. also any regulatory docs for the security team so we can prepare the SOC2 artifacts.
[02:41] Tom Reeves: I'll share traffic percentiles, current infra diagram, and list of sensitive prompt types.
[02:47] Alex Chen: Great. we'll follow up with a pricing sheet and proposed bench slots.
[02:51] Mark Daniels: One more on fallbacks: if a GPU node fails during peak, will traffic be routed to other instances and degrade gracefully? we can't have hard errors.
[02:59] Priya Rao: Smart routing will reassign requests and we can configure automatic fallback to a smaller model variant under load, reduced chunk sizes, or queuing behavior. can set SLA-based routing priorities too.
[03:12] Sara Liu: For embeddings cost, can you show cost per 1M vectors across instance types?
[03:16] Alex Chen: We'll include a cost matrix in the pricing sheet covering A100, H100-like configs and cheaper inference-optimized SKUs for embeddings.
[03:24] Tom Reeves: Ok that's helpful. let's get the bench scheduled and security docs shared.
[03:28] Alex Chen: Perfect. Priya will send a calendar invite for bench slots and a short runbook request.
[03:33] Mark Daniels: Thanks all.
[03:34] Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll send notes and action items.

(Transcript quality: medium - occasional word swaps and omitted filler words)

End of transcript.
